subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
title: Seasons in the County
overview: A season is a period of the year with its own kind of weather. This sub-strand is about four seasons: hot, cold, dry and rainy. You will learn how to recognise them in your county, how they change the work people do, how rain changes road safety, and how to show the seasons on a weather chart.

lessons.title: The four seasons and how to recognise them
objectives: Name the four seasons: hot, cold, dry and rainy.
Describe the signs of each season in your own county.
lessons.intro: Some mornings you need a jumper. On other days the sun is fierce by breakfast, or the road is wet before you leave home. Those differences are signs of the seasons.
lessons.notes:
A season is a stretch of weeks or months when the weather has a pattern. One cloudy afternoon is weather. A season is the bigger pattern. In this sub-strand we study four seasons:

- Hot
- Cold
- Dry
- Rainy

### Signs of each season
Hot season: the sun feels strong, the ground can be warm under your feet, and people look for shade. You feel thirsty more often.

Cold season: mornings and nights feel chilly. People wear warmer clothes. In highland parts of Kenya, cold can be sharp even when the afternoon becomes milder.

Dry season: little or no rain falls. Grass may turn brown, some streams become low, and dust rises on paths. Clothes put outside dry quickly.

Rainy season: rain falls often. The soil is wet, grass grows, and paths may be muddy. Water tanks and rivers can fill.

A place can feel more than one of these at the same time. A rainy day can also be cold, and a dry month can also be hot. We still use the four names because they help us describe what is happening.

### Your county is the place to watch
Kenya is a large country. The season you are in is not always the same as the season in a county far away. Some areas have long rainy periods and long dry periods. Highland areas can be cool when low, dry areas are hot. Do not copy another county's weather. Observe your own.

Keep a class record for two weeks: each school day, write hot or mild, wet or dry, and one thing you noticed, such as muddy shoes or a clear sky. Ask a parent or guardian, and look in a textbook or a trusted weather report, to find out which season the county is known for at this time of year. Seasons last longer than two weeks, so adults and books help you name the season, while your record helps you notice the signs.

When you report to the class, say "In our county at this time we notice..." and name the signs. That is how you identify the seasons where you live.

keyWords.meaning: a period of the year with a pattern of weather, such as rainy or dry
the state of the air at a particular time, such as sunny, rainy or windy

examples.problem: For three days the sky is cloudy, but no rain falls and the streams are low. Which season is this more likely to be: rainy or dry?
steps: A rainy season has rain and wet soil.
Low streams and no rain fit a dry season, even if clouds pass.

examples.problem: Why should you not assume that every county in Kenya is in the rainy season because your county is?
steps: Kenya's counties do not all have the same weather at the same time.
examples.answer: Different parts of Kenya have different weather. Identify the season by observing your own county.

activity.title: Brainstorm the seasons we see
materials: Textbook or other print resource on seasons
steps: In groups, brainstorm the seasons experienced in your county and the signs of each.
Check your ideas against a print or digital resource your teacher provides, and against what adults at home say.
Start a two-week class record of what you observe each school day.
Agree on which of the four seasons best matches the county at this time of year, and say which signs support the choice.

practice.question: Name the four seasons in this sub-strand.
What is the difference between weather and a season?
practice.answer: Weather is the condition at a particular time. A season is a longer pattern of weather.

practice.question: Give two signs of a rainy season.
practice.answer: Any two: rain falls often, the soil is wet, paths are muddy, grass grows, tanks and rivers fill.

summary: The four seasons we study are hot, cold, dry and rainy.
A season can share signs with another, such as cold and rainy.
Identify the season in your county by observation, adults and reliable resources.

lessons.title: How seasons influence what people do
objectives: Explain how hot, cold, dry and rainy seasons change human activities.
Give examples of activities from your own county.
lessons.intro: Farmers watch the sky before they plant. Families choose different clothes in a cold month from the clothes they wear in a hot month. The season influences, or affects, the work and habits of people.
lessons.notes:
Human activities are the things people do, such as farming, herding, going to school, trading, building and travelling. Seasons influence these activities because people need rain, warmth, dry ground or shelter at the right time.

### Hot season
People wear light clothes and drink water often. Hard outdoor work may be done early in the morning or later in the day, when it is cooler. Animals need shade and water. Food can spoil faster, so families keep it covered. Where the hot season is also dry, farmers may wait for rain before planting.

### Cold season
People wear warmer clothes, and families may light a fire that an adult watches. In cool highland areas of Kenya, crops such as tea are grown because they suit cool, wet slopes. Learners still come to school; they just prepare for a colder morning.

### Dry season
Many farmers harvest and dry grain in the sun. Herders may move animals to look for pasture and water if grass near home is finished. Water in rivers and pans can fall, so people use water sparingly. Dry roads are usually easier to walk and drive on than muddy ones. Dust can blow across a road, so road users still need to watch carefully.

### Rainy season
This is the main planting time in many farming areas, because seeds need moist soil. Grass grows, so animals have more to eat. Weeding follows planting. Too much rain can flood fields, delay building work, and make paths hard to use. School attendance can suffer if a road is cut, which is why road safety in the rain is a lesson of its own.

### Ask someone who works on the land
Invite a farmer, a herder or another adult, with your teacher's help, to explain how the seasons change their work in your county. Write what they say under the four headings. Their examples will fit your county better than a general list. Compare their answers with the points above and keep both: the general pattern, and the local example.

Activities change with the season, but people's needs do not disappear. Food, water, school and safety matter in every season. The season changes how the community meets those needs.

keyWords.meaning: the things people do, such as farming, herding, trading and going to school

examples.problem: A farmer in a crop-growing area is waiting to plant maize. Which season is the farmer most likely waiting for, and why?
steps: Seeds need moist soil.
The rainy season provides that moisture in many farming areas.
examples.answer: The rainy season, because the soil becomes moist enough for seeds.

examples.problem: Give one human activity that is easier in the dry season than in heavy rain.
steps: Think of drying crops or using roads.
examples.answer: Drying harvested grain in the sun, or travelling on firm roads.

activity.title: Seasons and people's work
materials: Four heading cards: Hot, Cold, Dry, Rainy
A visitor such as a farmer or herder, if the teacher can invite one
steps: Brainstorm human activities you see in the county.
Sort them under the season when they are most common.
If a resource person visits, ask how each season changes their work, and record the answers.
Each group explains one season to the class with a local example.

practice.question: Why do many farmers plant during the rainy season?
practice.answer: Seeds need moist soil, and rain wets the soil.

practice.question: Give one way a hot season influences daily life.
practice.answer: People wear light clothes, drink more water, seek shade, or do hard work during cooler parts of the day.

practice.question: What may herders do in a dry season if pasture near home is finished?
practice.answer: Move animals to look for pasture and water.

practice.question: Why is a local farmer a useful person to ask about seasons?
practice.answer: The farmer can explain how seasons change work in your own county.

summary: Hot, cold, dry and rainy seasons change farming, herding, dress and travel.
Planting often depends on rain, and drying grain is easier in dry weather.
Local adults can explain how these patterns work in your county.

lessons.title: Rainy weather and road safety
objectives: Explain how rainy weather makes roads less safe.
State precautions road users should take in the rain.
lessons.intro: Rain fills tanks and helps crops, and it also changes the journey to school. A path that was firm yesterday can be slippery today, and a familiar dip in the road can hide under a puddle.
lessons.notes:
Road users are people who walk, cycle, ride or drive on a road. In the rainy season they all face extra dangers. Knowing the dangers helps you reach school safely and helps you value the rainy season without being careless in it.

### What rain does to a road
- Mud and water make the surface slippery, so walkers fall and vehicles take longer to stop.
- Potholes fill with water. A shallow-looking puddle may be a deep hole.
- Flood water can cover a road or a bridge. It may be deeper and faster than it looks, and it may sweep a person off their feet.
- Heavy rain makes it hard for drivers to see people.
- Lightning can strike tall objects in an open place.

### Precautions for learners
- Wear bright clothes so that you are easier to see. A raincoat or an umbrella helps, but an umbrella must not block your view of traffic.
- Use the pavement or the edge of the road, and face oncoming traffic if you must walk on the road.
- Cross at a safe place, look both ways, and walk. Do not run out from behind a vehicle.
- Hold an adult's hand when you can.
- Do not play in flood water. It is dirty and it hides holes.
- Do not walk, cycle or drive through water covering a road or bridge. Turn back and tell an adult.
- If lightning is close, go inside a building. Do not shelter under a single tall tree.
- Allow more time for the journey.

Drivers and riders should slow down, switch on lights, and avoid splashing walkers. You can remind adults in your family of these points.

### Other seasons have safety rules too
In the hot season, drink water and do not stay in a closed hot vehicle. In the cold season, dress warmly. In the dry season, watch for dust and for animals crossing roads as herders move them. The rainy season needs the longest list because water changes the road so quickly.

Appreciating the rainy season includes being glad of water for farms and still choosing the safe way to travel. Talk in groups about one dangerous spot on the way to your school and what learners should do there when it rains.

keyWords.meaning: an action you take beforehand to stay safe
anyone who walks, cycles, rides or drives on a road
water that covers land which is usually dry

examples.problem: A puddle lies across your usual path to school. What is the safe choice?
steps: Rain can hide a deep pothole.
Do not walk through flood water.
examples.answer: Go around it on safe ground, or turn back and tell an adult if the water covers the road. Do not wade through it.

examples.problem: Why should you wear bright clothes on a rainy morning?
steps: Drivers find it harder to see in the rain.
examples.answer: Bright clothes help drivers and riders see you.

activity.title: Rainy-day safety talk
materials: A simple sketch of the road near the school
steps: Discuss ways rainy weather affects walkers, cyclists and drivers.
Mark one dangerous spot on a sketch of the journey to school.
Agree on precautions for that spot.
Role-play a learner helping a younger child to cross safely in the rain.
List one safety precaution for the hot season, the cold season and the dry season as well.

practice.question: Give two ways rainy weather makes a road less safe.
practice.answer: Any two: the road is slippery, potholes are hidden, floods may cover the road, drivers cannot see well.

practice.question: What should you do if flood water covers the bridge you usually use?
practice.answer: Do not cross. Turn back and tell an adult.

practice.question: Where should you go if lightning is close?
practice.answer: Inside a building. Do not shelter under a single tall tree.

summary: Rain makes roads slippery, hides holes and can cause floods.
Walkers should be visible, avoid flood water, and cross carefully.
Being glad of rain includes travelling safely in it.

lessons.title: Weather charts of the seasons
objectives: Make a weather chart that shows the four seasons in your county.
Record human activities and sing about the seasons you experience.
lessons.intro: A chart turns a long explanation into a picture the whole class can read. When the seasons change, you can point to the chart and see what people do, and how they stay safe, in each one.
lessons.notes:
A weather chart of the seasons is a table or a poster that shows the four seasons side by side. Modelling the chart means you design it, make it, and use it, not only copy a drawing from the board.

### What to put on the chart
Give the chart a title, such as "Seasons in our county". Use four columns or four boxes:

- Season: Hot, Cold, Dry, Rainy
- Signs: what you see and feel
- Human activities: what people do
- Safety: one precaution

Draw a simple symbol for each season: a sun, a jumper, cracked dry ground, and rain clouds. Colour the boxes. Leave a strip at the bottom labelled "This month in our county" and pin a movable card there. Move the card when the class agrees that the season has changed.

Use your two-week observation record and the notes from the resource person. If a box would only be a guess, write what you have observed or been told, and leave a question mark on anything not yet confirmed.

### Recording activities
Beside the chart, keep a second sheet: "Activities we have seen". Each week, add one activity you observed, such as planting, drying maize, wearing warm clothes, or collecting water. This sheet links the season to real life in the county.

### A song
Singing helps the class remember the four seasons. Use a tune you already know and these words, or write your own:

Hot season, we drink and keep in the shade.
Cold season, we dress so we do not fade.
Dry season, we save the water we store.
Rainy season, we plant, and we walk with care once more.

Sing together. Patriotism here is pride in understanding your home area, including its weather.

Display the chart in the learning corner. When a new learner asks what the weather is like in your county, take them to the chart and explain one season in your own words. Updating the chart through the year is how you appreciate the different seasons instead of ignoring them.

keyWords.meaning: a table or poster that shows seasons, their signs and what people do
a simple drawing that stands for something, such as a cloud for rain

examples.problem: Name the four headings that a season box on the chart should include.
steps: Look at the plan: season, signs, activities, safety.
examples.answer: The name of the season, the signs, the human activities, and a safety precaution.

activity.title: Model a seasons chart
materials: Cards for the movable season marker
steps: Draw a chart with the four seasons and columns for signs, human activities and safety.
Fill the boxes from your observations and from what a resource person or textbook has confirmed.
Add symbols and a movable card showing the season in the county now.
Record one human activity you have seen this week.
Sing a song about the four seasons and display the chart.

practice.question: What four seasons should appear on your weather chart?
Why does the chart have a safety line for each season?
practice.answer: Each season has precautions, especially the rainy season for road users.

practice.question: What should you do with a fact you have not confirmed?
practice.answer: Leave a question mark or check it before writing it as a fact.

practice.question: Give one reason for singing about the seasons.
practice.answer: The song helps the class remember the four seasons and what people do in them.

summary: A seasons chart shows signs, activities and safety for hot, cold, dry and rainy seasons.
Fill it from observation and from confirmed local information.
A song and a display help the class appreciate the seasons in the county.

quiz.question: Which set names the four seasons in this sub-strand?
quiz.explanation: The four seasons are hot, cold, dry and rainy.

quiz.question: Which observation best fits a dry season?
options: Rain every afternoon and muddy paths
Little rain, brown grass and low streams
Snow on every road in Kenya
quiz.explanation: A dry season has little rain. Streams fall and grass may turn brown.

quiz.question: Why do you observe your own county instead of copying another county's weather?
quiz.answer: Different parts of Kenya can be in different seasons at the same time.
quiz.explanation: A season must be identified where you live.

quiz.question: Why do many farmers plant in the rainy season?
quiz.explanation: Rain wets the soil so that seeds can grow.

quiz.question: What may herders do when pasture finishes in the dry season?
quiz.answer: Move animals to look for pasture and water.
quiz.explanation: Dry weather reduces grass and water near home.

quiz.question: Which danger comes with rainy weather on the road?
options: Roads become slippery and puddles can hide holes
Traffic lights stop working in every county
The sun rises in the West
quiz.explanation: Rain makes surfaces slippery and hides potholes.

quiz.question: Flood water covers the bridge on your way to school. What should you do?
options: Turn back and tell an adult
quiz.explanation: Flood water can be deeper and faster than it looks.

quiz.question: What should a seasons chart include for each season?
quiz.answer: The season name, signs, human activities and a safety precaution.
quiz.explanation: Those four parts make the chart useful.

quiz.question: Which symbol best matches the rainy season on a chart?
quiz.explanation: A rain cloud stands for rainy weather. The chart can also show activities and safety.

quiz.question: Which sentence shows appreciation of the seasons in your county?
options: I learn the signs of each season and travel safely in the rain.
quiz.explanation: Appreciation includes noticing the seasons and acting safely.
